_about: Free aerial imagery sources for the address-first site start. Both tools/aerial.py and the layout tool (AERIAL_SOURCES block, copied by tools/sync_rules.py) read this table. Each source is an ArcGIS REST service: type image = ImageServer exportImage, map = MapServer export. bbox = [west, south, east, north] lon/lat coverage (null = US/world). gsd_ft = nominal ground sample distance; a catalog or metadata query replaces it with the value at the site. license: public = public domain or CC0, free for engineering use with credit; restricted = view and trace only, check the provider's terms before issuing a drawing with it (off unless asked). Add a state or county source by adding an entry; probe it with python3 tools/aerial.py --list.
_sources_checked: 2026-10-23: USGS NAIP Plus catalog fields (live), SANDAG SD2023_9inch item info (public domain per SanGIS/Nearmap agreement; 3 in is partners only), Ohio OSIP most current, Indiana current imagery (CC0, 6 in 2025), CT Ortho 2023, Esri World Imagery and its metadata service (SRC_DATE, SRC_RES). Hosts other than imagery.nationalmap.gov are not yet allowed in the cloud environment. 2026-10-23 (second pass, from service directories found by web search, not probed from the cloud): Cook County 2024/2025, DRAPP 2022 (Jeffco portal, CC BY 3.0; no 2024 service found), City of Boulder 2024, Missouri 6 in 2023-24, NYS ITS Latest (covers NYC), NJ 2020, Fairfax 2023. Not added: Colorado statewide Vexcel (government only), MassGIS 2023 (tile layer on tiles.arcgis.com, export not supported), Texas StratMap (per-project services).
